A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same density-estimation and InPCA study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations and figures are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLaMA-2 density-estimation trajectories, fitted-kernel results and comparisons with classical estimators on Gaussian, uniform and randomly generated distributions.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds Gemma/Mistral comparisons, heavy-tailed targets, alternative-distance embeddings and histogram-prior experiments.

M1.justification: Serialization, Hierarchy-PDF, InPCA and the two-parameter bespoke KDE remain. However, v1 specifies Hellinger-distance fitting; v3 retains that objective in Equation 9 while Appendix A.12 identifies KL-divergence as the fitting loss. This inconsistency prevents determining whether the fitting objective actually changed.

E1.justification: v3 Appendix A.10 adds heavy-tailed Student's t targets with degrees of freedom 0.1, 1 and 2, evaluated using LLaMA-2 13B and Mistral-7B-v0.3. Gaussian, uniform and Gaussian-process-generated targets remain, within the same univariate unconditional density-estimation task.

E2.justification: The cross-model comparisons expand beyond LLaMA-2 to Gemma-2B, Gemma-7B and Mistral-7B-v0.3, including comparisons with their bespoke-KDE counterparts in Figures 12–13. Figure 2 replaces the LLaMA-2 7B/70B examples with Mistral/Gemma examples, while Appendix A.3 retains the original LLaMA comparisons. Classical KDE and histogram comparators remain.

E3.justification: Added analyses use Bhattacharyya and symmetrized-KL embeddings, including an imaginary third component, and histogram priors alpha = 0.1, 1 and 2 with 500 observations (Appendices A.6 and A.11). These are additional protocols; the retained main experiments still use two-digit inputs, 100 bins and 200 observations.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands checks on the interpretation: cross-family bespoke-KDE replication, sensitivity to statistical distance, heavy-tailed targets and histogram-prior strength (Appendices A.4, A.6, A.10–A.11). These supplement, rather than replace, v1's PCA comparison, kernel-shape analyses, random-target experiments and Silverman-bandwidth check.

E5.justification: Both versions already report inverse-Hessian parameter uncertainties. v3 changes the stated Hessian loss from Hellinger distance to KL-divergence and adds Appendix A.12 explaining the uncertainty calculation. It does not document additional repeated runs or introduce seed-based uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds cross-family trajectory and kernel-fit findings, alternative-distance results (Figure 15 reports 90% Bhattacharyya and 87% symmetrized-KL preservation), heavy-tail convergence results and prior-sensitivity curves. It also changes the zero-context narrow-uniform density/kernel snapshot from v1 Figure 22 to v3 Figure 25. Most original results remain; these additions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.12 adds a derivation connecting the KL Hessian, Fisher information and parameter covariance under close-fit and regularity assumptions. Appendix A.6 develops signed-embedding reasoning. Existing KDE and bandwidth mathematics remain. The new covariance display inconsistently equates covariance with Fisher information despite the surrounding inverse-Fisher explanation.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements broaden the shared-trajectory and adaptive-KDE claims from the LLaMA-2 suite to LLaMA-2, Gemma and Mistral. The central contributions—probing density estimation, visualizing learning geometry and proposing a kernel interpretation—remain the same.

C2.justification: v3 adds speculation about a universal cross-family density-estimation algorithm, explains apparent non-convergence through imaginary embedding coordinates, and interprets heavy-tail instability and the histogram prior's smoothness/convergence tradeoff. The dispersive-induction-head hypothesis and existing qualifications about imperfect KDE imitation remain.

D1.justification: The v3 abstract newly supplies a repository location for code and a 3D visualization. Appendix A.4 identifies the additional model checkpoints and their tokenizer compatibility with Hierarchy-PDF. Existing serialization and random-distribution generation details are retained; repository availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting Gemma, Mistral, Student's t distributions, Minkowski-space discussion and Fisher-information reasoning. The established positioning relative to synthetic-trained in-context learners, classical density estimation and prior InPCA research remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing prose remain. Edits generalize LLaMA-specific terminology, refine wording and cross-references, update author/publication information, and insert or rename appendix subsections. The scientific additions do not accompany a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn with different model examples, density snapshots and trajectories. New Figures 12–13, 15 and 38–39 add cross-family, alternative-distance, heavy-tail and prior-sensitivity displays, including imaginary-coordinate visualization. Existing figures are largely retained but relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the central empirical interpretation by testing whether it extends beyond one model family and survives changes in distance measure, target tails and histogram priors. These directly address alternative explanations for v1's findings, and the code-access disclosure improves reproducibility information. The conflicting fitting-loss descriptions and erroneous covariance equality weaken the new uncertainty treatment, but the broader, targeted validation provides a substantial net gain.
